entry.title: Tabular foundation models, from my AI Austria talk

link.title: Tabular foundation models, from my AI Austria talk

entry.content:
TL;DR. Tabular foundation models do for tables what in-context learning does for text. You hand over labelled rows, and one forward pass answers the query rows. There is no training on your data and no hyperparameter search. This post collects the slides, the notebook and the papers from my talk at the AI Austria GenAI Community, Codeforce Edition on 30 September 2026.

What the talk covered

Three parts. First, what a tabular foundation model is and how it differs from a large language model. Second, why prescriptive maintenance needs more than a good prediction, and how a causal foundation model answers “what if” questions while the line stands still. Third, a live notebook in which TabICL and a random forest compete on hand-drawn data and on a maintenance benchmark.

Slides and notebook

Slides and the hands-on notebook follow here after the talk.

Start here

  • C. Molnar: Tabular Foundation Models, a free online book with runnable examples. The best entry point.
  • N. Hollmann et al.: Accurate predictions on small data with a tabular foundation model, Nature 2025. TabPFN v2, the paper that made the field visible.
  • J. Qu et al.: TabICLv2: A better, faster, scalable, and open tabular foundation model, ICML 2026. The open model used in the notebook.
  • A. Pfefferle et al.: nanoTabPFN, a TabPFN in under 500 lines that you can pre-train yourself in minutes.

How it works

  • S. Müller et al.: Transformers Can Do Bayesian Inference, ICLR 2022. Prior-data fitted networks, the idea behind all of these models.
  • N. Hollmann et al.: TabPFN: A Transformer That Solves Small Tabular Classification Problems in a Second, ICLR 2023. The first tabular foundation model.
  • T. Nagler: Statistical Foundations of Prior-Data Fitted Networks, ICML 2023. Why a forward pass can approximate Bayesian inference.
  • J. Qu et al.: TabICL: A Tabular Foundation Model for In-Context Learning on Large Data, ICML 2025.

Code to play with

  • TabICL: open weights, scikit-learn API, runs on a laptop.
  • TabPFN by Prior Labs, with the TabPFN-3.5 technical report.
  • nanoTabPFN and TFM-Playground: small, readable implementations to learn from.
  • modded-nanoTabPFN: the pre-training speedrun, from 74 minutes to under one minute on one GPU (paper).
  • NVIDIA structured-data-models: one GPU-native API for TabICLv2, Kumo Tabular, TabFM and the relational model KumoRelational, released with the Kumo Tabular announcement.
  • Google TabFM, also available in BigQuery.
  • drawdata and marimo, the tools behind the drawing demo.

Benchmarks

  • TabArena: the living leaderboard for tabular machine learning (paper).

Tabular foundation models for maintenance

  • R. Theiler et al.: Towards Unified and Data-Efficient Prognostics and Health Management with Tabular Foundation Models, 2026.
  • C. Li et al.: Small data challenges for intelligent prognostics and health management: a review, Artificial Intelligence Review 2024.

From prediction to decision

  • J. Robertson et al.: Do-PFN: In-Context Learning for Causal Effect Estimation, 2025.
  • Y. Ma et al.: Foundation Models for Causal Inference via Prior-Data Fitted Networks, 2025.
  • M. Doutreligne and G. Varoquaux: How to select predictive models for decision-making or causal inference, GigaScience 2025.

My work

  • F. Saretzky et al.: Integrating a Causal Foundation Model into a Prescriptive Maintenance Framework for Optimising Production-Line OEE, Procedia CIRP 2026.
  • M. Orošnjak, F. Saretzky, S. Kędziora: Prescriptive Maintenance: A Systematic Literature Review and Exploratory Meta-Synthesis, Applied Sciences 2025.
  • F. Saretzky, T. Engel, F. Ansari: Network-based Root Cause Identification to Improve OEE in High-Precision Manufacturing, IFAC-PapersOnLine 2025.
  • ProductionLineSimulator: synthetic production lines with causal ground truth, as used to pre-train PriMa-Causa.

entry.title: Literature research with Claude and Zotero

link.title: Literature research with Claude and Zotero

entry.content:
Status: supported · Confidence: high · Last checked: 2026-10-30

TL;DR. Three parts: an agent, skills that teach it literature search, and your Zotero library with a semantic index. Set up once in about 30 minutes, and Claude does most of it for you. Then you ask in plain language and get answers that cite papers you can open.

flowchart LR
  you([You]) --> agent
  subgraph agent [Agent]
    cc[Claude Code]
    cs[Claude Science]
  end
  agent -- loads --> skills
  agent -- calls --> zmcp
  subgraph skills [Skills: know-how]
    s1[literature-search-arxiv]
    s2[literature-search-openalex]
    s3[literature-review]
  end
  skills --> web[(arXiv, OpenAlex, Crossref<br/>what is new)]
  zmcp[Zotero MCP<br/>access] --> lib[(Zotero library<br/>what you have)]
  zmcp --> idx[(Semantic index<br/>full text, local)]

Why bother

Today With the setup
Keyword search in Scholar, then again in Zotero One question searches both
“I read this somewhere”, title forgotten Found by what the paper claims
Chatbots invent references Every citation is a retrieved record with a DOI
Paper in one window, its code in another One session reads both and compares them

Three terms

Agent. Claude that acts: it runs searches, reads files and executes code, instead of only chatting.

Skill. A folder with a text file SKILL.md: a name, a one-line description, instructions, often scripts. Think of a shelf of lab protocols: the agent reads only the labels on the spines. When a task matches a label, it takes that protocol down and follows it. So a skill takes up no room in the agent’s working memory until it is needed.

MCP. The Model Context Protocol, a plug that connects the agent to a program, here Zotero.

A skill says how to do something. MCP gives access to something.

sequenceDiagram
  participant You
  participant Agent
  participant Skill as SKILL.md
  participant OA as OpenAlex
  Note over Agent: sees only names and descriptions
  You->>Agent: What is new on X since 2024?
  Agent->>Skill: description fits, read it
  Skill-->>Agent: steps, rules, a script
  Agent->>OA: run the script
  OA-->>Agent: papers with DOI and citations
  Agent-->>You: answer with checked citations

The head of a real skill from Google DeepMind, abridged:

---
name: literature-search-arxiv
description: Search for scientific papers, preprints, and publications on arXiv.
  Use when the user asks to find research papers, literature, or specific arXiv IDs.
---

# arXiv Search and Retrieval

Maximum 1 request every 3 seconds. Always use the provided scripts.

Why embed the library

Keyword search needs the words. You remember the claim. An embedding model turns every passage of every PDF into a vector that encodes its meaning. Your question becomes a vector too, and the nearest passages win.

flowchart LR
  q["How are synthetic pretraining<br/>distributions designed?"]
  q --> kw[Keyword search] --> miss[No hit:<br/>title shares no word]
  q --> sem[Semantic search] --> hit[Hit: the passage<br/>in the paper you meant]
  • Meaning over wording. The query above found the paper I had in mind. Its title shares no word with the query.
  • Passages, not titles. The index covers full texts in chunks, so a match lands on a page.
  • Local. The index is built and stored on your machine, with a free embedding model that runs there too. Only passages the agent opens go to Claude.
  • Yours first. The library holds what you already judged worth keeping. The literature skills fill the gaps.
flowchart LR
  pdf[PDFs in Zotero] -- passages --> emb[Embedding model<br/>on your machine]
  q[Your question] --> emb
  emb -- vectors --> db[(Vector index)]
  db -- closest passages --> agent[Agent reads<br/>and cites]

Pick a route

flowchart LR
  start{Your main work?} -- "papers, writing, code" --> A[Route A: Claude Code<br/>in the Claude app]
  start -- "lab data, life sciences" --> B[Route B: Claude Science app]
  Claude Code Claude Science
What Code tab of the Claude desktop app Research workbench app, in beta
Setup One prompt, Claude installs the rest A few clicks in Settings, plus four commands
Literature skill arXiv and OpenAlex skills from Google DeepMind Built-in literature review; a reviewer agent checks citations
Best for Any field, code, LaTeX, your own files Life sciences, analyses with figures and provenance
Plan Claude Pro or higher Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise; macOS and Linux

Step 1: Let Zotero talk

Both routes need this one click. Zotero 7 or newer: Settings → Advanced, tick Allow other applications on this computer to communicate with Zotero.

Route A: Claude Code in the Claude app

No terminal needed. Claude Code runs the setup commands itself and asks before each one.

  1. Install the Claude desktop app, sign in, open the Code tab and pick a folder to work in.

  2. Paste this prompt:

    Set me up for literature research with my Zotero library:
1. Install zotero-mcp-server (github.com/54yyyu/zotero-mcp)
   with semantic search, use the free local embedding model
   and build the index over the full texts.
2. Connect it to Claude Code as a user-level MCP server
   named zotero, with ZOTERO_LOCAL=true.
3. Install the skills literature-search-arxiv,
   literature-search-openalex and uv from
   github.com/google-deepmind/science-skills for Claude Code.
Explain each step in one sentence before you run it.
  3. Start a new session and test the whole chain: Search my Zotero library by meaning for a topic I know well. It should return papers with matching passages. A broken embedding model shows no warning, only empty or failed searches. Type / to see the skills.
Prefer to type it yourself? The same in a terminal 
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash        # Claude Code
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh       # uv
uv tool install "zotero-mcp-server[semantic]"
zotero-mcp setup --semantic-config-only               # 1 = free local model
zotero-mcp update-db --fulltext                       # build the index
claude mcp add zotero --scope user -e ZOTERO_LOCAL=true -- zotero-mcp
npx skills add google-deepmind/science-skills -g -a claude-code \
  -s literature-search-arxiv literature-search-openalex uv

For better search, still local: install Ollama, run ollama pull qwen3-embedding:0.6b and pick option 4 in zotero-mcp setup. Ollama then has to run whenever you search. If it does not, the search fails with “connection refused” on localhost:11434.

Route B: Claude Science

  1. Download Claude Science and sign in. On first start it asks which connectors and skills to turn on. Keep Literature review.

  2. Install zotero-mcp and build the index. Either let Claude Code do it (prompt step 1 above), or in a terminal:

    curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
uv tool install "zotero-mcp-server[semantic]"
zotero-mcp setup --semantic-config-only
zotero-mcp update-db --fulltext
  3. Connect Zotero: Settings → Connectors → Add connector → Local command. Name zotero, command /Users/<you>/.local/bin/zotero-mcp. Under Advanced settings add the environment variable ZOTERO_LOCAL=true.
  4. Optional, for arXiv: Settings → Skills → Add skill → Import from GitHub, then google-deepmind/science-skills.
  5. In a chat, type / and pick literature-review, or just ask. Claude loads the skill when the task fits.

The first index build takes a while for a large library. Later updates only add what changed.

Ask

sequenceDiagram
  actor You
  participant A as Agent
  participant Z as Zotero
  participant W as OpenAlex, arXiv
  You->>A: What is known about X?
  A->>Z: semantic search: what do I have?
  Z-->>A: passages from 6 papers
  A->>W: skill: what is new since 2024?
  W-->>A: 14 candidates with DOI
  A->>A: verify DOIs, read key passages
  A-->>You: synthesis with citations
  You->>A: add the best three to Zotero
  A->>Z: create items

Prompts that work:

  • Search my Zotero library first: what do I have on X? Then search OpenAlex for work since 2024 that I am missing. Cite with DOI.
  • Which paper in my library argues that Y? Quote the passage and give the page.
  • Compare what paper Z claims with what its GitHub code does.
  • Add the three most cited of these to my Zotero collection “Review 2026”. Writing needs a one-time zotero-mcp authorize-local.

Limits

  • Scanned PDFs without OCR return nothing.
  • The ranking is useful, the similarity score is not.
  • Full texts are expensive in context. Search to locate, read selectively.
  • The agent retrieves, you judge. Open every citation you keep.
  • Long Claude Science runs use up plan limits quickly.

Open: whether indexing what I already collected quietly narrows what I look for next.

Sources. Claude Code docs · Claude Science: connectors and skills · Google DeepMind science-skills · zotero-mcp · Model Context Protocol · Diagrams drawn with Pele
entry.summary: A visual setup guide. One question to an AI agent searches the papers you already have and the ones you are missing, and every answer cites a paper you can open.
